facts.statement: Campylognathoides lived in Germany during the Early Jurassic, specifically the Early Toarcian age.
facts.quote: Campylognathoides is an extinct genus of pterosaur discovered in the Württemberg Lias deposits (dated to the early Toarcian age) of Germany

facts.statement: The genus Campylognathoides was erected by Felix Plieninger based on better-preserved specimens found in the Holzmaden shale.
facts.quote: Felix Plieninger erected a new genus

facts.statement: Friedrich August Quenstedt originally named the species P. liasicus in 1858 based on wing bones found near Metzingen.
facts.quote: In 1858 Friedrich August Quenstedt named a new species of Pterodactylus: P. liasicus

facts.statement: Bernhard Hauff sr. discovered a large pterosaur skeleton near Holzmaden in 1893.
facts.quote: In 1893 commercial fossil collector Bernhard Hauff sr. discovered a skeleton of a large pterosaur near Holzmaden

facts.statement: Felix Plieninger established the genus Campylognathus in 1894 using the specimen discovered by Bernhard Hauff sr.
facts.quote: In 1894 Felix Plieninger based a new genus on this specimen: Campylognathus

facts.statement: The genus name Campylognathus means "bent jaw" in Greek, referring to the animal's lower jaw structure.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek kampylos, "bent", and gnathos, "jaw", in reference to the bent lower jaw

facts.statement: Felix Plieninger corrected Quenstedt's identification in 1901, proving that the bone thought to be a coracoid was actually a short metacarpal.
facts.quote: In 1901 Plieninger for the first time studied P. liasicus and discovered that Quenstedt had mistaken the, in reality short, metacarpal, for a coracoid

facts.statement: Plieninger recognized a second species, C. liasicus, in 1907 and assigned the Carnegie Museum specimen CM 11424 to it.
facts.quote: In 1907 however, Plieninger recognised a second species of Campylognathus: C. liasicus, to which CM 11424 was referred also

facts.statement: The type species C. zitteli from Holzmaden had a wingspan of 1.75 meters.
facts.quote: The larger Holzmaden Campylognathoides, C. zitteli (SMNS 9787), had a wingspan of 1.75 m

facts.statement: C. liasicus had a wingspan of three feet, making it smaller than C. zitteli.
facts.quote: C. liasicus had a three foot wingspan, making it smaller than its Holzmaden contemporary, C. zitteli

facts.statement: Kevin Padian considers C. indicus a nomen dubium, suggesting it might be based on a fish fossil rather than a pterosaur.
facts.quote: Kevin Padian considers this a nomen dubium, possibly based on a fish fossil

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that Campylognathoides had acute vision or a nocturnal lifestyle due to its large, low-placed eye sockets.
facts.quote: The large eye sockets, placed low in the skull above a narrow jugal, have caused some researchers to speculate that Campylognathoides had especially acute vision, or possibly even a nocturnal lifestyle

facts.statement: The snout of Campylognathoides ended in a slender point that curved slightly upward.
facts.quote: The snout ends in a slender point curving a bit upwards at its very end

facts.statement: The teeth were conical and recurved with a broad base and a beveled inner point forming a sharp cutting surface.
facts.quote: They are conical and recurved but have a broad base with the point bevelled off from the inside forming a sharp and strong cutting surface

facts.statement: The maximum total number of teeth in Campylognathoides is 66.
facts.quote: The largest total number is thus 66

facts.statement: The tail had a flexible base with six short vertebrae followed by elongated, stiffened vertebrae that allowed the tail to function as a rudder.
facts.quote: The tail base is flexible with about six short vertebrae; behind them the caudals elongate and are stiffened by very long extensions allowing the tail to function as a rudder

facts.statement: The sternum was a large rectangular bone plate featuring a short forward-facing crest called a cristospina.
facts.quote: The sternum of Campylognathoides was a rather large rectangular plate of bone with a short forward-facing crest called a cristospina

facts.statement: Despite short metacarpals, the wing was long due to an exceptionally long second wing finger, the largest phalanx in the hand.
facts.quote: The lower arm too is short but wing length is considerable due to the hand, which has short metacarpals but a very long wing finger for a basal pterosaur, of which the second phalanx is the largest

facts.statement: The upward-lateral position of the hip socket suggests Campylognathoides walked quadrupedally and could not stand erect on its hind legs.
facts.quote: This would prove that Campylognathoides was not well able to walk on its hind legs but must have walked quadrupedally

facts.statement: In 2009, Padian argued that an erect posture was necessary for fast locomotion, creating a debate over whether the animal walked quadrupedally or bipedally.
facts.quote: However, Padian in 2009 concluded the opposite, stating that an erected position was necessary to place the feet on the ground and that, though a quadrupedal gait was possible, a bipedal way of locomotion was a precondition for a fast gait

facts.statement: Campylognathoides had relatively short legs and small feet.
facts.quote: The leg is rather short and the feet are small

facts.statement: The fifth toe was exceptionally short for a basal pterosaur, though it was often interpreted as supporting an interdigital membrane.
facts.quote: The fifth toe, often interpreted as carrying a membrane between the legs, is exceptionally short for a basal pterosaur

facts.statement: In 2003, David Unwin and Alexander Kellner established the clade Campylognathoididae for this genus.
facts.quote: In 2003 both David Unwin and Alexander Kellner introduced a clade Campylognathoididae

facts.statement: Campylognathoides is considered the most basal member of the Novialoidea clade.
facts.quote: Campylognathoides is the basalmost member of the Novialoidea

facts.statement: Evidence from gut contents indicates that Campylognathoides ate the belemnoid cephalopod Clarkeiteuthis conocauda.
facts.quote: Direct dietary evidence based on gut contents suggests that Campylognathoides fed on a belemnoid cephalopod Clarkeiteuthis conocauda

facts.statement: Campylognathoides, meaning "curved jaw," is a rhamphorhynchoid pterosaur discovered in Lias deposits in Württemberg.
facts.quote: Campylognathoides ("mandíbula curvada", Strand 1928) es un género de pterosaurio "ranforrincoide", descubierto en los depósitos del Lias de Württemberg

facts.statement: Felix Plieninger established the new genus based on better-preserved specimens found in the Holzmaden shale.
facts.quote: fue basándose en dichos especímenes que Felix Plieninger designó un nuevo género

facts.statement: The genus name Campylognathus is derived from Greek words meaning "curved" and "jaw," referring to its curved lower jaw.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego kampylos, "curva", y gnathos, "mandíbula", en referencia a su mandíbula inferior curvada

facts.statement: Norwegian entomologist Embrik Strand found in the 1920s that the name Campylognathus was already used for an African beetle, leading him to rename the pterosaur.
facts.quote: El entomólogo noruego Embrik Strand descubrió en la década de 1920 que el nombre Campylognathus ya se había usado previamente para el escarabajo africano Campylognathus nigrensis

facts.statement: Embrik Strand renamed the pterosaur Campylognathoides in 1928.
facts.quote: renombró al pterosaurio Campylognathoides en 1928

facts.statement: The first specimen of Campylognathoides consisted of wing fragments.
facts.quote: consistiendo el primer espécimen en fragmentos del ala

facts.statement: New discoveries have increased the number of known specimens to nearly a dozen.
facts.quote: Durante el nuevos hallazgos han elevado el número de especímenes conocidos a cerca de una docena

facts.statement: Campylognathoides had a relatively short snout but an elongated skull with a lighter constitution compared to its contemporary Dorygnathus.
facts.quote: El hocico en este género es relativamente corto, aunque el cráneo es aún alargado, pero de constitución más ligera.

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that Campylognathoides had exceptionally sharp vision or a nocturnal lifestyle based on its large, low-set eye sockets.
facts.quote: Las grandes cuencas oculares, situadas bajas en el cráneo sobre un estrecho hueso yugal, han hecho que algunos investigadores especulen que Campylognathoides haya tenido una visión especialmente aguda, o incluso un estilo de vida nocturno.

facts.statement: The snout of Campylognathoides ended in a thin tip that curved slightly upward at the front.
facts.quote: El hocico finaliza en una punta delgada curvándose un poco hacia arriba en su extremo frontal.

facts.statement: A small triangular opening called the antorbital fenestra was located below the large bony nostrils in the skull.
facts.quote: Bajo éstas se encuentra una pequeña abertura triangular en el cráneo, la fenestra antorbitalis.

facts.statement: Campylognathoides teeth were conical and recurved with a wide base and beveled tips forming a sharp, strong cutting surface.
facts.quote: Estos son cónicos y recurvados pero tienen una base amplia con la punta biselados desde el interior formando una afilada y fuerte superficie cortante.

facts.statement: The total number of teeth in Campylognathoides was 66.
facts.quote: El número total de dientes es entonces 66.

facts.statement: Campylognathoides had a flexible tail base with about six short vertebrae followed by long, rigid vertebrae that allowed the tail to function as a rudder.
facts.quote: La base de la cola es flexible con cerca de seis vértebras cortas; detrás de éstas las caudales son alargadas y rígidas a través de muy largas extensiones permitiendo a la cola tener una función de timón.

facts.statement: The sternum of Campylognathoides was a large rectangular bone plate with a short forward-facing crest called the cristospina.
facts.quote: El esternón de Campylognathoides era una lámina grande rectangular de hueso con una corta cresta vuelta hacia adelante llamada cristospina.

facts.statement: Although Campylognathoides had a short forearm, its wing length was considerable due to a hand with short metacarpals and a very long wing finger where the second phalanx was the longest.
facts.quote: El antebrazo también es corto pero la longitud del ala es considerable debido a la mano, la cual tiene cortos metacarpos pero un muy largo dedo del ala para un pterosaurio basal, del cual la segunda falange es el más largo.

facts.statement: The fifth toe of Campylognathoides, often interpreted as holding a membrane between the legs, was exceptionally short for a basal pterosaur.
facts.quote: El quinto dedo del pie, que frecuentemente se interpreta sujetando una membrana entre las patas, es excepcionalmente corto para un pterosaurio basal.

facts.statement: A fossil collector found a well-preserved Campylognathoides pelvis in a slate quarry in Braunschweig, Germany, in 1986.
facts.quote: Un coleccionista de fósiles encontró una cadera de Campylognathoides bien preservada en una cantera de esquistos en Braunschweig, Alemania en 1986.

facts.statement: Campylognathoides zitteli, described by Plieninger in 1894, is the type species of the genus.
facts.quote: Campylognathoides zitteli (Plieninger, 1894) es la especie tipo.

facts.statement: Campylognathoides liasicus was originally described by Quenstedt in 1858 under the name Pterodactylus liasicus.
facts.quote: Campylognathoides liasicus (Quenstedt, 1858 [originalmente Pterodactylus liasicus])

facts.statement: Campylognathoides indicus was described by Sohan Lal Jain in 1974 based on a jaw fragment found in the Chanda district of India.
facts.quote: "Campylognathoides" indicus (Jain, 1974) C. indicus fue descrito por Sohan Lal Jain sobre la base de un fragmento de una mandíbula, ISI R. 48, recuperada en el distrito de Chanda, en la India.

facts.statement: Kevin Padian considers Campylognathoides indicus a nomen dubium, possibly based on a fish fossil.
facts.quote: Kevin Padian lo considera un nomen dubium, posiblemente basado en un fósil de pez.

facts.statement: Fossil sites of Campylognathoides were located in the early Jurassic north of the Bohemian Massif island, situated in a shallow gulf of the Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: El área de los sitios fósiles estaba localizado a principios del Jurásico al norte de una gran isla, el Macizo de Bohemia, situado en un golfo poco profundo del mar de Tetis.

facts.statement: Campylognathoides lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: A quadrupedal posture has been confirmed in other rhamphorhynchoid pterosaurs besides Campylognathoides.
facts.quote: Esta postura también ha sido confirmada en otros "ranforrincoides" (pterosaurios primitivos).

facts.statement: In 2009, Padian concluded that an upright posture was necessary for foot placement and that bipedal locomotion was a precondition for speed, despite the possibility of quadrupedalism.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Padian en 2009 concluyó lo opuesto, estableciendo que una postura erguida era necesaria para situar el pie en el suelo y que, aunque una postura cuadrúpeda era posible, una forma bípeda de locomoción era una precondición para un andar rápido.

facts.statement: The debate over whether Campylognathoides was primarily quadrupedal or bipedal remains highly controversial.
facts.quote: Esta cuestión sigue siendo altamente controversial.

facts.statement: Kevin Padian suggested that Campylognathoides may have been a predator of small terrestrial animals due to its short, strong teeth ideal for piercing bites.
facts.quote: Padian sin embargo, ha sugerido que en vista de sus dientes cortos y fuertes, ideales para dar una mordedura de perforación, bien pudo haber sido un depredador de pequeños animales terrestres.

facts.statement: The specialized fish-eating niche may have been filled by Dorygnathus, which is five times more common in these strata than Campylognathoides.
facts.quote: El nicho del especializado devorador de peces pudo haber sido llenado por Dorygnathus el cual es cinco veces más común en estos estratos.

facts.statement: In 2003, David Unwin and Alexander Kellner introduced the clade Campylognathoididae, which Unwin placed as the sister taxon to Breviquartossa within Lonchognatha, while Kellner placed it as the most basal branch within Novialoidea.
facts.quote: En 2003 tanto David Unwin como Alexander Kellner introdujeron el clado Campylognathoididae; dentro de la terminología de Unwin este clado es el taxón hermano de los Breviquartossa dentro de Lonchognatha; aplicando la terminología de Kellner es la ramificación más basal dentro de los Novialoidea.

facts.statement: A 2010 analysis by Brian Andres showed that Eudimorphodon and Austriadactylus formed a basal clade, leaving Campylognathoides as the only known member of Campylognathoididae.
facts.quote: En 2010 un análisis publicado por Brian Andres mostró que Eudimorphodon junto con Austriadactylus formaban un clado muy basal, dejando a Campylognathoides como el único miembro conocido de los Campylognathoididae.

facts.statement: The largest Campylognathoides from Holzmaden, C. zitteli, had a wingspan of 1.8 meters.
facts.quote: El mayor Campylognathoides de Holzmaden, C. zitteli, tiene una envergadura de 1,8 metros.

facts.statement: C. liasicus had a wingspan of 91 centimeters, making it smaller than its contemporary C. zitteli from Holzmaden.
facts.quote: C. liasicus tiene una envergadura de 91 centímetros, lo que lo hace menor que su contemporáneo en Holzmaden, C. zitteli.

facts.statement: In 2008, Padian noted that the difference in wing length between species might result from ontogenetic development, as larger individuals would need larger wings to limit wing loading.
facts.quote: En 2008 sin embargo, Padian señaló que esto pudo haber sido resultado del desarrollo ontogénico, ya que los individuos grandes necesitarían alas mayores para limitar la carga alar.

facts.statement: In his later publications, Plieninger assigned Campylognathus to the superfamily Rhamphorhynchoidea.
facts.quote: Plieninger en sus últimas publicaciones asignó a Campylognathus a los "Rhamphorhynchoidea".

facts.statement: Assigning Campylognathus to Rhamphorhynchoidea simply established the negative fact that it was not a pterodactyloid, as that superfamily was a paraphyletic collection of unrelated basal pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Como este suborden es una colección parafilética de pterosaurios basales no especialmente relacionados entre sí, esta clasificación simplemente establece el hecho negativo de que no era un pterodactiloide.

facts.statement: In 1974, Peter Wellnhofer concluded that Campylognathoides was situated in a more basal position on the phylogenetic tree, below Rhamphorhynchidae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1974 Peter Wellnhofer concluyó que estaba situado en una posición más basal en el árbol filogenético, bajo los Rhamphorhynchidae.

rejected.statement: Embrik Strand renamed the pterosaur Campylognathoides in 1928 because the name Campylognathus was already taken by an African bug genus.
rejected.quote: Norwegian entomologist Embrik Strand discovered in the 1920s that the name Campylognathus had previously been used for the African bug Campylognathus nigrensis

rejected.statement: C. indicus was described by Sohan Lal Jain in 1974 based on a jaw fragment found in Chanda district, India.
rejected.quote: C. indicus was described by Sohan Lal Jain on the basis of a fragment of jaw, ISI R. 48, recovered from Chanda district, India

rejected.statement: In 2008, Padian suggested that differences between species might be due to ontogeny, where larger individuals grew larger wings to reduce wing load.
rejected.quote: However, in 2008 however, Padian pointed out that this might well have been a matter of ontogenetic development, larger individuals growing extra large wings to limit the wing load

rejected.statement: C. liasicus had 12 to 14 teeth in the lower jaw, while C. zitteli had 16 to 19.
rejected.quote: In the lower jaw there are twelve to fourteen teeth present in C. liasicus, sixteen to nineteen in C. zitteli

rejected.statement: A study by Kevin Padian identified 8 cervical, 14 dorsal, 4 or 5 sacral, and up to 38 caudal vertebrae.
rejected.quote: According to a study by Kevin Padian there are eight cervical vertebrae, fourteen dorsals, four or five sacrals and up to 38 caudal vertebrae

rejected.statement: In 1967, Oskar Kuhn placed Campylognathoides in its own subfamily, Campylognathoidinae, within Rhamphorhynchidae.
rejected.quote: Después de un período en que se efectuó muy poco trabajo sobre la sistemática de los pterosaurios, en 1967 Oskar Kuhn situó a Campylognathoides en su propia subfamilia dentro de Rhamphorhynchidae, los Campylognathoidinae.
